item.title: How WA colleges are preparing for ICE
item.description: There have been no documented instances of federal immigration enforcement taking place on Washington’s public college campuses.

item.title: President Donald Trump’s post-State of the Union sales job begins now
item.description: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump has delivered the State of the Union. Now the challenge for him is to make that message stick.

item.title: Bill and Hillary Clinton, battle-tested, gear up for another Washington fight
item.description: WASHINGTON — For some of their conservative critics, this is the scandal that could finally topple them. Their resistance to testifying proved futile. And now, staring down another epic fight, they're harnessing their considerable political skills to try and turn the table on their accusers.

item.title: Bill Gates apologizes for Epstein ties, admits to affairs with Russian women
item.description: NEW YORK — Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates issued an apology for his ties to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein during a townhall for the Gates Foundation, during which he also confessed to having two affairs while married to his ex-wife, Melinda French Gates, according to reports.

item.title: Mariners’ Cal Raleigh not focused on another 60-HR season
item.description: Cal Raleigh has already gone deep this spring, yet the switch-hitting Seattle Mariners catcher isn’t focused on trying to hit 60 home runs again this season.

item.title: Vance says administration is pausing some Medicaid funding to Minnesota because of fraud concerns
item.description: WASHINGTON — Vice President JD Vance announced Wednesday that the Trump administration would “temporarily halt” some Medicaid funding to the state of Minnesota over fraud concerns, as part of what he described as an aggressive crackdown on misuse of public funds.

item.title: Lawsuit filed on behalf of 8 juveniles alleges ‘culture of abuse’ at Clark County Juvenile Justice Center between 1978 and 2014
item.description: A Vancouver law firm has filed a lawsuit on behalf of eight juveniles against Clark County, alleging staff at the county’s juvenile detention facility sexually abused detainees over the span of decades.

item.title: Jenna Klopman of Washougal girls basketball is The Columbian 2025-26 Week 16 prep athlete of the week sponsored by Killer Burger
item.description: Klopman received 192 of the 402 votes cast last week to win the honor.

item.title: Woodland man in court in death of Vancouver woman whose body was found in Yacolt Burn State Forest
item.description: A Woodland man is being held without bail after he allegedly killed a 34-year-old Vancouver woman and dumped her body in the Yacolt Burn State Forest in east Clark County.

item.title: No. 9 Gonzaga beats Portland 89-48 to clinch WCC crown
item.description: Graham Ike scored 19 points and matched a school record with seven steals as No. 9 Gonzaga routed Portland 89-48 to clinch its first West Coast Conference regular-season championship in three years.
